subject.title: Telegram getUpdates 409 cascade after IPv6→IPv4 transport fallback; rebuild loop self-perpetuates without canceling in-flight long-polls

question: Should the remaining Telegram 409/fallback work be solved primarily as token-level polling lifecycle recovery under #75852, as an operator IPv4 pin surface like #78438, or as both?
rationale: The source shows partial mitigations but no live proof of full recovery, and adding a new network/env surface is a product and compatibility choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Prioritize lifecycle fix
options.body: Keep #89954 open as the IPv6-triggered slice and drive the durable fix through #75852 so one bot token cannot self-overlap getUpdates across restart, timeout, and fallback paths.

options.title: Accept IPv4 pin mitigation
options.body: Proceed with an explicit FORCE_IPV4-style operator escape hatch after maintainer approval, tests, and documentation, while leaving lifecycle recovery tracked separately.

options.title: Close after live main proof
options.body: Close only if a maintainer can reproduce the affected broken-IPv6 multi-account setup on current main and show the 409 cascade no longer occurs.

recommendation.title: Prioritize lifecycle fix
recommendation.body: Keep #89954 open as the IPv6-triggered slice and drive the durable fix through #75852 so one bot token cannot self-overlap getUpdates across restart, timeout, and fallback paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-history owner for both the fallback-chain and 409 conflict restart paths involved in the decision.
